claims.text: Wear resistance of the HEA coating will initially increase as ambient temperature rises.
The initial improvement in wear resistance persists up to approximately 400–600 °C.
Formation of a protective surface oxide layer causes the elevated-temperature improvement in wear resistance.
Tribological performance degrades rapidly above the critical temperature threshold.
High-temperature degradation is caused by thermally activated diffusion-induced microstructural coarsening and loss of solid-solution hardening.
The initial coating is dense and nanocrystalline or fine-grained.
The initial HEA coating has high hardness and a single-phase or multiphase solid-solution structure with high lattice distortion.
The relevant structural mediators are the evolving tribo-oxide layer and the stability of the underlying precipitate or matrix microstructure.
At moderately elevated temperatures, oxidation produces a continuous, adherent, and self-healing oxide film.
The oxide film lowers the coefficient of friction.
The oxide film prevents direct metal-to-metal contact.
At higher temperatures, the sluggish-diffusion effect is overcome.
Coarsening of strengthening precipitates reduces yield strength through the Orowan mechanism.
High-temperature phase instability causes oxide spallation or substrate softening and leads to abrasive-wear dominance.
Wear rate decreases from room temperature to about 600 °C and then increases sharply above about 600 °C.
At room temperature, the coating typically has moderate wear because a fully developed protective oxide layer is absent.
For many Al-containing HEAs, the degradation boundary lies between 600 and 800 °C.
The degradation boundary occurs when significant precipitate coarsening begins or oxide adhesion falls below the sliding-interface shear stress.
Refractory HEAs may retain performance to higher temperatures, although their use is limited by poor high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The transition temperature depends strongly on alloy composition, coating grain size, precipitate volume fraction, and deposition method.

contradictions.description: The critical threshold is stated as approximately 400–600 °C in the hypothesis and about 600 °C in the predicted outcome, whereas the boundary field places degradation between 600 and 800 °C. These overlapping but materially different ranges leave the proposed boundary internally inconsistent.
